title: Reported speech 1 (he said that ...)
subtitle: Paul said that he was feeling ill.
summary: Report what somebody said with said/told + that, moving the verb one step into the past.

lesson.heading: Two ways of reporting
lesson.text: You saw Paul yesterday and you want to tell somebody what he said. Paul's words were: *'I'm feeling ill.'* You can repeat his exact words (direct speech), or you can report them (reported speech).

examples.text: *reported:* Paul said that **he was feeling** ill.

lesson.heading: The verb goes back into the past
lesson.text: When we use reported speech, the main verb of the sentence is usually past (*Paul said that ... / I told Lisa that ...*). The rest of the sentence is usually past too. You can leave **that** out.

examples.text: Paul said **that** he was feeling ill.
Paul said he was feeling ill.
I told Lisa that **I didn't have** any money.

lesson.heading: Anna's words, reported later
lesson.text: You met Anna and she told you several things. Later you tell somebody else what she said.

examples.text: 'I've lost my phone.' - Anna said that **she had lost** her phone.
'I want to buy a car.' - She said that **she wanted** to buy a car.
'I can't come to the party on Friday.' - She said that **she couldn't come** to the party on Friday.
'My parents are fine.' - She said that **her parents were** fine.
'I'll phone you when I get back.' - She said that **she would phone** me when **she got** back.

lesson.heading: The past simple can stay the same
lesson.text: The past simple (*did / saw / knew*) can stay the same in reported speech, or you can change it to the past perfect (*had done / had seen / had known*). Both are correct.

examples.text: *direct:* Paul said: 'I woke up feeling ill, so I didn't go to work.'
*reported:* Paul said he **woke up** feeling ill, so he **didn't go** to work.
*reported:* Paul said he **had woken up** feeling ill, so he **hadn't gone** to work.

lesson.text: Watch the pronouns as well as the verbs: *'You can borrow mine'* becomes *Kate said I could borrow hers*.

exercises.prompt: Paul said, 'I'm feeling ill.' Later you say: Paul didn't go to work today. He said he ___ ill.
exercises.explanation: am/is becomes was, so am feeling becomes was feeling.

exercises.prompt: Tom said, 'It's too far. Let's get a taxi.' Later you say: I wanted to walk to the station, but Tom said ___ too far.
exercises.explanation: is becomes was in reported speech.

exercises.prompt: Anna said, 'I don't want to go.' Later you say: Anna has been invited to the party but she told me ___ to go.
exercises.explanation: don't becomes didn't in reported speech.

exercises.prompt: Dan said, 'I'll let you know next week.' How do you report this?
options: He said he would let me know next week.
He said he will let me know next week.
He said he let me know next week.
exercises.explanation: will becomes would after a past reporting verb.

exercises.prompt: Ben said, 'I haven't seen her for a while.' Later you say: I asked Ben about Rachel, but he told me ___ her for a while.
exercises.explanation: have/has becomes had, so haven't seen becomes hadn't seen.

exercises.prompt: Anna said these things. Match each one with its reported form.

pairs.right: Anna said that she had lost her phone.
She said that she wanted to buy a car.

pairs.left: 'I can't come to the party on Friday.'
pairs.right: She said that she couldn't come to the party on Friday.
She said that she didn't have much free time.
She said that her parents were fine.

exercises.prompt: Kate said, 'You can borrow mine.' Later you say: I needed to borrow a guitar and Kate said ___ hers.
exercises.explanation: can becomes could, and you/mine become I/hers.

exercises.prompt: Sue said, 'I'm not enjoying it very much.' Later you say: I asked Sue about her job. She said ___ it very much.
exercises.explanation: am not becomes wasn't, so I'm not enjoying becomes she wasn't enjoying.

exercises.statement: James said, 'I sold my car a few months ago.' Reported: He told me that he sold it a few months ago.
exercises.explanation: Correct. The past simple can stay the same, or you can say he had sold it.

exercises.prompt: Sarah said, 'I don't know.' Report what she said.
exercises.answer: She said that she didn't know.
exercises.explanation: don't becomes didn't; that is optional but here it is one of the chunks.

exercises.prompt: Amy said, 'There are twenty students in my class.' Later you say: I asked Amy about her school and she told me ___ twenty students in her class.
exercises.explanation: are becomes were, and my becomes her.

exercises.prompt: What does each direct-speech form become in reported speech?
